AGREEMENT
ARTICLE I
RECOGNITION AND JURISDICTION

A. The Employer recognizes IF&CWU Local No. 408 as the exclusive and collective bargaining agent for all employees working in the Meat Department at all of Employer's retail stores located in the following counties: Arenas, Austin, Bastrop, Bell, Brazos, Galveston, Grimes, Hardin, Harris, Jasper, Jackson, Jefferson, Polk, Liberty, Walker, Lee, Liberty, Matagorda, Milam, Montgomery, Nacogdoches, Orange, Panola, Polk, Refugio, San Jacinto, San Patricio, Jefferson, Winn, Tyler, Victoria, Walker, Walker, Wharton, Washington, and Wharton. The parties agree that this Contract shall cover, the Union which is a party hereto, shall have jurisdiction over all Meat Department employees of the Employer who are, or will be, owned or leased, operated by the Employer in such counties.

It is hereby agreed that the terms and provisions of this Agreement shall be binding upon the successors and/or assigns of the Employer. In the event of a change in ownership of the operation, the Company shall pay off all obligations under this Agreement to the Union and the employees.  The Company shall pay monetary benefits due employees under the terms of this Agreement at the time of transfer of ownership.

B. For the purpose of this Contract, the Meat Department includes all employees who are engaged in the handling, processing, and offering for sale of fresh meat, poultry, processed poultry, fish, rabbits, sausages, smoked meats and meat products, which has customarily been performed by bargaining unit employees in the stores continuing within the jurisdiction of the Union, regardless of the bargaining unit's current composition, (1) to the extent such functions continue to be performed by the Employer, (2) to the extent such work is performed by the Employer, (3) in the Union's geographical area of representation as set forth above, and (3) to the extent such work is not currently represented by another Union. Specifically, although some duties previously performed by bargaining unit employees in designated geographical areas are covered by this Agreement, the Employer will continue to recognize the Union and work's collective bargaining jurisdiction over the Employer's store delicatessen operations that existed prior to the execution of this Agreement. If the Employer decides to open a delicatessen in any of the counties in the markets may continue to do so to the extent this service are presently performed.

C. It is not intended by any provision of this Agreement to prevent the Employer from cutting, packaging or otherwise handling meat dining at any central point. The Employer agrees that any work of cutting, packaging or otherwise handling meat at any central point owned, leased, or operated by the Employer in the counties listed in Paragraph A above which was previously performed by bargaining unit employees shall remain the work of the employees of this bargaining unit under the wages, hours and working conditions of this Contract, except where this work is under the jurisdiction of an existing collective bargaining contract with the Employer. New classifications may be established as necessary. The Employer agrees that the establishment of new positions shall not prematurely embrace work being performed by employees in any established classification. Prior to establishing such a new classification, the Employer and the Union shall confer to establish the wage rate for such classification. In the event the parties cannot agree after such conference, the Employer may establish such a new classification and rate.

ARTICLE II
NON-DISCRIMINATION—CHECK-OFF

A. There shall be no discrimination against any employee, whether by the Employer or the Union, because of their membership or nonmembership in the Union.

B. The Employer and the Union agree that neither shall discriminate against any employee because of age, race, creed, color, sex or national origin. It is understood that wherever there appears a reference in this collective bargaining agreement to male or female gender, the intent is to interpret such reference as applying to both males and females.

C. The Employer shall, during the term of this Contract, deduct finition fees and regular union dues weekly from employees who are members of the Union and who individually and voluntarily certify in writing authorization for such deductions. The Employer shall remit all sums deducted in this manner to the Union.

A uniform Active Labor Ball dutuction will be made in January of each year for those employees who indicate, in writing, year authorization to do so, and forwarded will be to the Local Union.

D. It is agreed that the Company will not attempt in any manner to prevent or discourage any employee from joining the Union or engaging in any lawful activity associated therewith. The Company agrees to tell new employees that they are operating under a Union contract.

E. Employers with facilities and capabilities, which have no employee credit union, agree to make weekly deductions in amounts designated by employees belonging to the UFCW Local Union No. 408 Federal Credit Union who desire to see such deductions and shall remit these amounts to such credit union.

ARTICLE III
NO STRIKE—NO LOCKOUT

A. The Union agrees not to cause, ratify or sanction any strike, slowdown, or stoppage of work and the Employer agrees that there shall be no lockout of any employees during the term of this Contract.

B. The Employer agrees that nothing in this Contract shall require any employee to report or perform to any work when do so will require her to access a legal prob job picket line in a primary labor dispute involving the Employer wherein the Union has sanctioned such a picket.  In order to be eligible, however, that UFCW Local No. 408 agrees that it will give the Employer at least forty-eight (48) hours notice after such primary picket simmering commences of its intention to sanction any such primary picket picket line.
